speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there will be a review on the coverage adequacy of MediShield Life to ensure that patients get appropriate treatment; and (b) whether more advisory support can be provided for policyholders, especially seniors, in the selection and scope of coverage for Integrated Shield Plan to minimise unnecessary coverage and to ensure that they have adequate health insurance coverage to pay for their medical bills when they need it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It is designed to cover the vast majority – nine in 10 – of subsidised bills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: More details will be available when the review is completed later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Notwithstanding the review of MediShield Life, many Singaporeans will still choose to buy additional private health insurance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: IPs provide greater coverage on top of MediShield Life, mainly to cover expenses for unsubsidised care in public hospitals or in private hospitals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Some will also choose to buy riders, which can further reduce cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, many people pay for protection that they do not use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These patients may not need IPs or riders, because MediShield Life is generally sufficient for such episodes and will be further enhanced after the major review this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, premiums for IPs and riders charged by private insurers are getting more and more expensive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will do more to help consumers understand their needs and choose the right health insurance to buy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Today, the Central Provident Fund (CPF) website and MoneySense, Singapore’s national financial education programme, already have educational articles on what to consider before buying an IP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is in addition to existing resources on MOH’s website which compare the benefits, features and premiums of IPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We can support individuals in making more informed health insurance decisions and will be working with CPF Board and the Life Insurance Association Singapore to achieve this.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As the Minister of State has mentioned, people will still buy IPs and it is not just for private healthcare.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Many of my residents have shared with me that they buy IPs because of sometimes long wait times and capacity, and to give them that choice to be able to shorten the wait times.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Because the care at our restructured hospitals and our public hospitals are actually very good, but the demand is also very high.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, the capacity issue does incentivise them to want to buy IPs in order to have that ability to shorten some of the wait time, not just to see a specialist but also for scans and tests.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, what can be done on the other end to help people who do not actually want IPs but have MediShield Life, to be able to get more timely care in terms of tests, scans and all that, given the capacity at our public hospitals?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The second question is with regard to the advisory on IPs because as rightly pointed out, IPs are very complex.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Apart from the information that is published, would there be any possibility for additional help in terms of an advisory panel that people can call up, besides the agents that they are buying from, to be able to say, "Am I over-insuring myself?"

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I acknowledge the concerns on the consumption of the public healthcare services, and the limitations and the capacity of the same.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As Members are already aware, there are a lot of efforts that we are making in trying to improve the capacity in the public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And thirdly, we are also looking at right-siting so that we do not tax the acute healthcare sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: All in all, there are multiple issues relating to the healthcare sector and there are a lot of issues people are concerned with and we are taking a multi-pronged approach, focusing various efforts on various fronts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I think the key thing is also related to the second point, it is in creating awareness and understanding of the choices for people to make because what we are seeing right now is that they are over-insuring and I think that is where the cost issue arises.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it relates to the Member's second point in that we really do need to enhance consumer education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are already platforms now and the exercise of CPF Board to provide information, comparison between different IPs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think more can be done in the community also to create such awareness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will take note of the feedback and point that the Member has suggested in the advisory committee, but I think the resources currently available are quite extensive and will actually help guide people in making decisions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Perhaps community partners can also step up to assist and support in enhancing the awareness of some of these resources available to the community.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have residents worried whether insurers sold them insurance premiums, while knowing the plans might rise and be in the long term not sustainable and that the policyholders may actually give up their premiums before making use of the benefits.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Then Senior Minister of State, Dr Koh Poh Koon, had said MOH would study it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The issue of portability had previously been explained by Minister Ong in a different setting.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Portability is a very complex matter and it may have unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
